issue.title: ACE agents loader 'disk' stage is p50 2.250s of a 3.284s visible_ready and no startup budget model attributes it
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and filed by sase-k3.land. Deliberately NOT one of the six follow-ups named in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md -- it is what the epic's re-measurement discovered was left over, which is why sase-k3.6 recorded it on its own bead instead of filing it.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. Epic sase-k3 removed persisted diff-badge classification, hidden-row repair, and a double ProjectSpec parse from ACE first paint. Real-terminal A/B (n=8 at baseline 59967cc06 vs n=9 at master 1f388edee, athena at loadavg ~30/64 cores, 33 agent rows / 532 index rows, initial_tab=agents) moved visible_ready p50 4.573s -> 3.284s and p95 6.327s -> 3.575s. The plan's target was p50 <2s / p95 <2.5s, so it missed by 1.28s / 1.08s even after deflating for host load.

THE GAP. After the epic, the agents loader's 'disk' stage is p50 2.250s of that 3.284s visible_ready -- the single largest remaining cost, and the epic's budget model does not account for it. The model attributed badges (~0.40s) and hidden-row repair (~0.26-0.39s) inside that stage, and both are now gone. Component measurement on athena at 1f388edee: the Tier-1 cached index query is only 0.280-0.464s of the stage, and a full load_agents_from_disk_with_state() call warms to 0.81-0.94s on repeat in the same process. That leaves roughly 1.3-1.9s of first-call loader work -- candidates named by the reporter are the dismissed-bundle snapshot, the Patch snapshot, and normalization/status overrides -- which neither the plan nor any of the three research passes ever measured.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the next thing to attack if the <2s visible_ready target still matters; nothing else in the remaining follow-up set is anywhere near 1.3-1.9s.

SCOPE. (1) Attribute the 'disk' stage: instrument the loader's first call so each component (dismissed-bundle snapshot, Patch snapshot, normalization, status overrides, Tier-1 query) reports its own span, rather than projecting from static analysis -- the epic's phase 'repair' was under-projected ~4-5x and phase 'axe' over-projected ~6x, so component estimates are not acceptable evidence here. (2) Attack whatever the attribution actually shows. (3) Accept on a real-terminal before/after of visible_ready_seconds from ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl per the recipe in docs/perf_runbook.md ('Startup telemetry capture'), not on component sums.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT INHERITED FROM THE EPIC: every figure above is warm-cache and was captured on a loaded host; see task sase-kj, which owns the cold-cache measurement that could reorder this ranking.
